text:
dinesh: Heads up — after rolling Cilium v1.16 to the us-west GPU clusters (gpu-pool-{a,b,c}) we started seeing increased east-west jitter and intermittent packet drops between worker pods. Hitting distributed PyTorch jobs (NCCL) — rings keep timing out and jobs stalling.

maria: When did the rollout finish? any deploy bot logs?

infra-bot: cilium-1.16.0 rollout completed in namespace kube-system on 1768502000 (canary->stable).

dinesh: Rollout finished ~1768502000 yes. Symptoms: pod->pod pings that were ~0.5ms baseline now spike to 20-60ms intermittently, and we see 0.1-0.5% packet loss on NCCL ports. Small control plane traffic ok. Only east-west (node-to-node) seems impacted.

choi: Can you paste `kubectl get pods -o wide` + Cilium status from affected nodes?

dinesh:

# kubectl -n kube-system exec -it cilium-xxxxx -- cilium status
KVStore:                Ok   Backends: etcd: 3/3
Cilium:                 Ok
Operator:               Ok
EndpointStatus:         214/220
HostRoutingTable:       Ok
ClusterMesh:            Disabled

# ip -s link show cilium_vxlan
3: cilium_vxlan: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes  123456789 packets 100234 errors 12 dropped 5
    TX: bytes  98765432 packets  98230 errors 8 dropped 3

maria: errors + dropped look suspicious. Any kernel logs?

dinesh:

# dmesg | tail -n 40
[ 12345.678901] vfio-pci 0000:03:00.0: disabled GSO on virtual function: GSO segmentation failed
[ 12346.001234] net_eth0: TX failed -63

choi: That looks like a GSO/GRO offload issue after encapsulation change (vxlan) — large frames are being segmented unexpectedly. Cilium v1.16 changed tunnel handling defaults in some installs; maybe GSO is not getting re-enabled on the vxlan device. RDMA/large-packet paths on our NICs don't like the fallback fragmentation.

leo: Repro steps locally? Can we isolate to one node pool and flip tunnel to "none" to test?

dinesh: I spun up a canary: patched Cilium configmap on gpu-pool-b nodes to `tunnel: none` and restarted cilium-agent on those nodes. After that, pod pings returned to ~0.6ms and NCCL jobs resumed normally on that pool. So disabling vxlan fixed it in the short term.

maria: Good quick mitigation. What's the impact to network policy and cross-node traffic when we disable tunnels? Do we have L2 adjacency between NICs across racks?

choi: For our setup, host routing + BGP fabric handles east-west without tunnel on the GPU VPCs, so tunnelless works here (but not in all regions). Tradeoff: more host routing entries and slightly more control-plane churn during node churn.

leo: Options: 1) Roll back to cilium 1.15.5 in prod (fast but loses other fixes). 2) Globally set `tunnel: none` for GPU pools (safer but environment-specific). 3) Wait for upstream patch (Cilium team said theyre looking at GSO on vxlan). Which do we prefer for a 2-hour mitigation window?

dinesh: My vote: targeted rollback for gpu clusters in us-west and toggle `tunnel: none` on remaining GPU nodepools as a safety net. I can run rollback in staging first.

maria: +1. Schedule: rollback in staging now, then prod rollback for gpu pools in 30m if green. Notify workloads + jobs owners (ml-platform).

infra-bot: Runbook step: helm rollback cilium 2 -n kube-system --dry-run recommended before actual.

dinesh:

# rollback test in staging
helm -n kube-system rollback cilium 2 --kube-context=staging
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status daemonset/cilium
# verify pings
kubectl exec -n test -it podA -- ping -c 100 podB

choi: Also capture `ethtool -k` on cilium_vxlan and underlying NIC before/after to include in postmortem. Example:

ethtool -k eth0
Features for eth0:
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on (disabled by device)
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on

maria: I opened an internal ticket and pinged the Cilium Slack/maintainers with our logs and kernel messages. They acknowledged a potential regression around GSO handling with vxlan+accelerated NICs and are triaging.

leo: After rollback in staging, monitoring look good?

dinesh: Staging rollback -> p99 latency back to baseline, no packet drops, NCCL tests pass. I'll stage a prod rollback for gpu pools in 30m and apply `tunnel: none` as fallback if any pool still has issues.

maria: Notify ML infra and on-call SREs. Postmortem: include timeline, config diff, kernel dmesg, ethtool outputs, and exact rollout windows. Add cost note: running tunnel none probably reduces encapsulation overhead but increases route count — negligible cost change but operational complexity.

infra-bot: Action items created: INFRA-2321 (rollback prod gpu clusters), INFRA-2322 (postmortem + upstream issue link).

choi: If upstream releases a patch, we should test specifically: (1) vxlan + GSO on NICs, (2) tunnel=geneve, (3) kernel versions. Let's keep kernel pinned for these nodes until validated.

dinesh: Thanks all — executing rollback + will post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
